title: Her father and sister's interest in jazz
summary: Her doctor father, a pianist, admired the technique of jazz players and thought it would live; her sister played Gershwin at Newcomb.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What did your parents think of jazz? Your parents and their friends?

They were very interested in it. As I say, my father and mother belonged to a very musical crowd, and they were quite up-to-date. And they embraced that with any other music that happened to come along. They were interested in it and actually had big troller records for us with that music. And even had, we used to have groups of people to our house and have Perron over there to play for us. My father was always interested in listening to that music. He was a pianist himself. And he thought highly of their technique and was interested greatly in the movement.
And would you say he was interested in it as an art form for music? He had to come as entertainment.

Well, he was entertained by it, but my father went into anything in music more deeply than most people would for entertainment. And he really thought it was an era and something that would live. And he was very proud of the fact that it had mostly originated in his part of the world.
But his whole... Which part was it when you were born?
Oh, hey, what he was about... I imagined 30-something.
I think. When you were born? When I was born. So I would put him in... Maybe about 30. Put him in late 40s or early 70s.
No, not late 40s, did you say?
Late 40s or early 70s when you started going to parties and having parties that you have.
When can you remember his daughter having guys ran to the house or they used to...

Well, my father didn't necessarily have them. He just... He knew that we liked this group of Peron, and we had a crowd that would meet every Saturday and Sunday. He didn't actually ask them to come to the house, but he was interested when they were there. And if he was home, he was a doctor and was out of great deal. But whenever he was there, he listened very attentively to them and often had conversation with them on their different ideas of jazz because he was such a gifted pianist himself. And my sister was a very gifted pianist, and she was the best one who ever played jazz up at Newcomb. She had a concert of Gershwin, and she was a Gershwin exponent. I guess you could call Gershwin in the realm of jazz.
It's jazz, but not New Orleans.
